cues.text: Frame 0, the source's move in our art: the roof, close, filling the frame, with a caption box across the middle like a phone clip's: HAIL OR WEAR? / YOU CALL IT., the EXAMPLE tag on its own row. At 0.8 s a blinds cut to a tighter shot of the same shingles; at 1.6 s an iris to one round mark, big. The caption box sits at the top (design r0) and is drawn over both cuts. The caption box, EXAMPLE row included, stays up through both cuts.
The camera walks across the shingles: three round marks, one after another, each framed by white camera corners (no words). EXAMPLE.

A dime (a plain silver disc, no face, no text) slides in beside one mark, the same size. Then a push in on the mark's bare center: the granules gone, loose granules collecting at the drip edge. EXAMPLE.
A cut out to the whole roof: light streaks running downslope, curled tab edges with a shadow under each, small bare patches spread evenly. EXAMPLE.
Two shots side by side: VENT, with a dent; GUTTER, smooth. EXAMPLE under each shot. The only words drawn here are VENT and GUTTER.

A close two-shot at the foot of a ladder (design r0: not damage-or-not's driveway): the roof edge and the vent at the top, siding, the ladder; the homeowner (k.client) points up, her bubble: IT'S HAIL. EXAMPLE. No house number, street sign or yard sign.

Back on the one round mark, big. Two choice cards: HAIL and WEAR, a cursor moving between them twice a second, YOUR CALL? over them. No answer: both cards look the same and never change (no glow, lift or check); from the last word on the cursor rests centered between them, on neither (facts r0). The cards come up on "and you're the estimator", so they hold about 3 s (design r0). EXAMPLE.
